_comment: Acknowledged read-path budget breaches as measured on 2026-08-31 (GH #293).
These files are ALREADY over their declared budget. Failing the run on all of them
every night would make read-path-budget-sweep.mjs a permanently-red line, and this
suite has twice learned what that does: workflow-health-sweep flagged a dead watchdog
in 16 consecutive runs and nobody acted, because the same line was red every time.
So a known breach at a stable size is reported as acknowledged, not as a finding.
GROWTH beyond tolerancePct in read-path-manifest.json still fails -- which is the live
signal, because growth is the actual defect (the journal folder went 2.26 MB -> 4.90 MB
in a month while GH #123 sat open).
Shrink a file below its budget and it leaves this list. Re-add an entry only with a
measurement and a reason.
`sizes` is the other half, added 2026-09-01. `known` only ever held files ALREADY over
budget, and growth was only checked for those -- so a file under its budget was never
growth-checked at all. SKILL.md went 43 KB -> 78.5 KB in seven days under a 96 KB budget
and this sweep reported clean every night. `sizes` records the measured size of the
every-run files that are within budget, so the growth signal applies to them too.
Update an entry here only together with a deliberate, reviewed size change.
`offPath` is the third list, added 2026-09-01. These files match a glob but not its
`idPattern`, so no run reads them -- they were previously misreported as OVER-budget
journals, whose stated remedy (shrink the file) was the wrong action on a file nobody
opens. They are acknowledged rather than failing because the AGENT CANNOT CLEAR THEM:
removing a file is blocked by the agent-gate.md floor rule 'Outcome can result in
permanent data loss'. A finding no run can ever clear is the permanently-red line this
suite has twice been burned by. They print in full in their own section, so acknowledging
them does not hide them. Delete the file and remove its entry here.
RE-BASELINED 2026-09-01 (GH #291), and this is the 'deliberate, reviewed size change' the
paragraph above asks for -- so it is written down rather than done quietly. task-400.md
256.8 -> 272.0, task-451.md 73.8 -> 86.8 (it had just broken the +15% tolerance), and
task-463.md added at 192.2 KB (it was OVER and absent from this list entirely).
The reviewed change is NOT that the files got smaller -- they did not. It is that the READ
PATH is now bounded: SKILL.md reads journals through `oa-state.ps1 extract`, whose worst
measured output across all 239 live journals is 15.5 KB against a 24 KB ceiling, versus 272 KB
read whole. So a breach here no longer means 'a run will spend ~70K tokens on this file'; it
means 'this file is still growing and has no retention policy', which is GH #123, not #291.
Re-baselining stops that from being a permanently-red line while leaving the growth signal
fully armed: exceed +15% from these numbers and the sweep fails again.

offPath.task-249-DESKTOP-P9116M3.md: OneDrive sync-conflict copy, 2026-07-07. Holds a superseded v1 proposal (Seattle City Light TOU) not present in task-249.md; check before deleting.
offPath.task-292-DESKTOP-P9116M3.md: OneDrive sync-conflict copy, 2026-07-07. Verified 2026-09-01: zero lines absent from task-292.md, so it is redundant.
offPath.task-463-DESKTOP-P9116M3.md: OneDrive sync-conflict copy, 2026-08-31. Verified 2026-09-01: its only differing line is a SHORTER form of task-463.md line 8, so it is redundant.
